modify.note: Carry the OAuth client's public or confidential type through client creation, authorization, token exchange, and refresh. Expose the PKCE choice in the admin client form. Require a challenge for a public client and a matching verifier when exchanging its authorization code. Confidential clients must still authenticate with their secret and, if they opted into PKCE, also pass the verifier check. Keep the authorization code bound to the correct client and redirect URI and preserve the existing expiry and consumption behavior. Update the token and refresh handlers together. Follow this task's refresh contract: public clients, and confidential clients that used PKCE, supply the verifier on refresh, while confidential clients also supply their secret. Preserve enough server-side or token-bound context to enforce that contract. Accept the supported refresh-token input locations, return standard token fields and no-store headers, and retain compatibility for existing confidential clients that do not use PKCE.
